## What is GeneExprLupusMx?

`GeneExprLupusMx` is an R package with **transcriptomic (RNA-seq) data from Mexican women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and from healthy controls**. It is designed for research and teaching: besides the data, it includes step-by-step lessons to learn how to analyze them.

- **33 participants:** 10 healthy controls (`Ctrl`) and 23 patients with lupus (`SLE`).
- **3 cell types per participant:** monocytes, monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDC), and tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDC).
- **99 samples** in total (33 × 3).

The data come from the article:

> Hernández-Ledesma AL, Coss-Navarrete EL, *et al* (2026) [Gene expression profiling of dendritic cell tolerance dysfunction in women with systemic lupus erythematosus](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959/full). *Front. Immunol.* 17:1771959. [doi: 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959](https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959).

```{r overview, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Overview of the study and of the package contents."}
knitr::include_graphics("img/overview.png")
```

## Installation

Install the package from [GitHub](https://github.com/EveliaCoss/GeneExprLupusMx). Some lessons also use `DESeq2`, available on [Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DESeq2):

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "BiocManager", "tidyverse"))
remotes::install_github("EveliaCoss/GeneExprLupusMx")
BiocManager::install("DESeq2")
```

Once installed, load it:

```{r setup}
library(GeneExprLupusMx)
```

## What data does it contain?

The package includes three main datasets. They are available as soon as you load the package; there is nothing else to download.

| Object | What it contains | One row per | Size |
|--------|------------------|-------------|------|
| `filtered_txi` | RNA-seq counts quantified with Salmon and imported with `tximport` | gene | 21,718 genes × 99 samples |
| `metadata_cleaned` | Group, cell type, and clinical data for each sample | sample | 99 samples |
| `volunteer_info` | Age, diagnosis, treatments, and recruitment date | volunteer | 33 volunteers |

It also includes **reference gene lists** used by some lessons:

| Object | What it contains | Used in |
|--------|------------------|---------|
| `biotype_summary` | Biotype of each gene (protein-coding, lncRNA…) | Lesson 4 |
| `sle_genes` | Genes associated with lupus in the literature | Lesson 4 |
| `isg_genes` | Interferon-stimulated genes (Yu et al., 2025) | Lesson 4 |
| `moDC_genes` | Genes described in the differentiation from monocyte to moDC | Lesson 5 |
| `dc_genes` | Genes associated with dendritic cell differentiation | Lesson 5 |
| `tolDC_genes` | Transcriptional signature of tolerogenic dendritic cells (Robertson et al., 2021) | Lesson 6 |

It also includes **checkpoints**: objects that are built in one lesson and saved in the package so that the next lesson can start from there, without repeating the steps.

| Object | What it contains | Built in |
|--------|------------------|----------|
| `dds` | Filtered and normalized `DESeqDataSet` (13,596 genes × 99 samples); requires `DESeq2` | Lesson 2 |
| `zscore_mat` | Matrix of z-scores of VST expression, for *heatmaps* (13,596 genes × 99 samples) | Lesson 2 |
| `de_results` | SLE vs Ctrl differential expression results for each cell type (`DESeq2`) | Lesson 3 |
| `go_results` | Enriched functional terms of the DEGs (g:Profiler, version e113) | Lesson 4 |
| `de_celltype_results` | Differential expression of moDC and tolDC against monocytes, in controls and patients (`DESeq2`) | Lesson 5 |
| `go_celltype_results` | Enriched functional terms of those DEGs (g:Profiler) | Lesson 5 |
| `de_interaction_results` | `Group:Cell_type` interaction: genes whose change from monocyte to dendritic cell is different in patients (`DESeq2`) | Lesson 7 |
| `go_interaction_results` | Enriched functional terms of those genes (g:Profiler) | Lesson 7 |

A quick look at each one:

```{r}
dim(filtered_txi$counts)       # genes x samples
head(metadata_cleaned[, c("sample_ID", "Group", "Cell_type")], 3)
head(volunteer_info[, c("Volunteer_ID", "Group", "Age_years", "Time_of_recruitment")], 3)
```

### How are they related?

The three tables are connected through their identifiers. Each sample has a name such as `QR011_1`: the first part (`QR011`) identifies the volunteer and the final number identifies the cell type (`_0` = monocyte, `_1` = moDC, `_3` = tolDC).

```{=html}
<pre class="mermaid">
flowchart LR
  T["filtered_txi<br/>counts per gene"] -- "columns = sample_ID" --- M["metadata_cleaned<br/>one row per sample"]
  M -- "Volunteer_ID<br/>(prefix of sample_ID)" --- V["volunteer_info<br/>one row per volunteer"]
</pre>
```

```{r}
# The count columns are in the same order as the metadata rows
all(colnames(filtered_txi$counts) == metadata_cleaned$sample_ID)

# From sample to volunteer
sub("_.*", "", "QR011_1")
```

To learn about each column in detail, see the help pages: `?filtered_txi`, `?metadata_cleaned`, and `?volunteer_info`.

## Learning path

The lessons are designed to be followed in order, but each one can be read on its own.

```{=html}
<pre class="mermaid">
flowchart LR
  P["Get started<br/>(this page)"] --> L1["1. Meeting the participants:<br/>descriptive statistics"]
  L1 --> L2["2. From RNA-seq counts<br/>to data exploration"]
  L2 --> L3["3. Differentially<br/>expressed genes"]
  L3 --> L4["4. Biological functions<br/>of DEGs"]
  L4 --> L5["5. Differentiation of monocytes<br/>into dendritic cells"]
  L5 --> L6["6. The signature of tolerogenic<br/>dendritic cells"]
  L6 --> L7["7. Do patient and control cells<br/>differentiate in the same way?"]
</pre>
<script type="module">
  import mermaid from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs";
  mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: true });
</script>
```

| Lesson | You will learn to… | Data | Time |
|---------|---------------|-------|--------|
| [1. Meeting the participants](clinical_en.html) | Describe the cohort with descriptive statistics, tables, normality tests, and comparisons between groups | `volunteer_info` | 45 to 60 min |
| [2. From RNA-seq counts to data exploration](intro_RNAseq_en.html) | Import the counts, normalize them with `DESeq2`, explore genes, and make *heatmaps* and PCA | `filtered_txi`, `metadata_cleaned`, `volunteer_info` | 1 to 1.5 h |
| [3. Differentially expressed genes between patients and controls](l3_DEGs_en.html) | Validate cell types with biomarkers, run differential expression with `DESeq2`, and interpret volcano plots | `filtered_txi`, `metadata_cleaned`, `zscore_mat` | 1.5 h |
| [4. Biological functions of differentially expressed genes](l4_GOterms_en.html) | Run a functional enrichment analysis with g:Profiler, identify SLE and ISG genes, and interpret biological processes | `de_results`, `go_results`, `sle_genes`, `isg_genes`, `biotype_summary` | 1.5 h |
| [5. Differentiation of monocytes into dendritic cells](l5_DEGs_monocytes_diff_en.html) | Compare dendritic cells against monocytes, validate differentiation with known genes, and explore pathways and lipid metabolism | `de_celltype_results`, `go_celltype_results`, `moDC_genes`, `dc_genes` | 1.5 h |
| [6. The transcriptional signature of tolerogenic dendritic cells](l6_DEGs_tolDcs_en.html) | Evaluate tolDC with a published signature, combine z-scores and LFC, and choose the right reference for comparison | `tolDC_genes`, `de_celltype_results`, `zscore_mat` | 1 h |
| [7. Do patient and control cells differentiate in the same way?](l7_DEGs_between_groups_en.html) | Fit a model with an interaction, interpret a "difference of differences", and summarize the genes with Reactome processes | `de_interaction_results`, `go_interaction_results`, `zscore_mat`, `isg_genes` | 1.5 h |

Each lesson includes **challenges** with their solutions for practice, and ends by reproducing a supplementary figure from the article.

## How to cite

If you use these data, cite the original article:

> Hernández-Ledesma AL, Coss-Navarrete EL, *et al* (2026) [Gene expression profiling of dendritic cell tolerance dysfunction in women with systemic lupus erythematosus](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959/full). *Front.
